newsitem.title: UK: British budget deficit in line with expectations.
newsitem.headline: British budget deficit in line with expectations.

text.p: Britain's budget deficit was 2.6 billion pounds ($4.3 billion) in November, according to official figures published Tuesday, suggesting the government was on course to meet its full-year borrowing target.

The Office for National Statistics (ONS) said the November shortfall in the public sector borrowing requirement (PSBR), as the deficit is known, followed a net repayment of 4.4 billion pounds ($7.3 billion) in October.

The figures were in line with expectations and the Treasury said they indicated the government would meet its target of a 26.4 billion pound ($44 billion) deficit in the current financial year, which runs to April 5.

"If the figures for the rest of the fiscal year come in around the same level as last, the government should be on track to hit its forecast," said Andrew Snowball, British economist at the Cooperative Bank.

The cumulative deficit for the financial year to date was 13.9 billion pounds ($23.2 billion), including privatisation proceeds, well below the 22.4 billion pounds ($37.3 billion) the government had to borrow in the same months of 1995/96.
However, economists said that with an election looming by next May, the government might have difficulty reining in public spending by imposing unpopular expenditure cuts.
"The last three months of the year tend to be the toughest in terms of controlling public spending, so things could get worse," said David Philpotts, British economist at Schroders.
The PSBR figures followed a report from the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) on Monday, which said Britain had made slow process in consolidating its public finances.
"Significant further progress in delivering the planned reduction in public sector borrowing will be needed to achieve the government's medium-term balanced budget objective," the OECD said.
